User authorized September 19:\nbuild this milestone in parallel with Claude's SL-2 Python parser alignment.\nThe final parity gate depends on that alignment; independent implementation\nand arena validation do not. This milestone changes the prototype only.\n\n## Scope\n\nReplace expression/block recursion with explicit continuations before admitting\nordinary `if condition { ... }`, optional `else { ... }`, and `else if` chains.\nAn if is an expression, usable in a binding, return, assignment RHS, argument,\noperator operand, condition, or block tail; the existing block statement/tail\nrules still apply. Branches contain the existing M20 statements and nested ifs.\nOptional binding (`if let`/`if var`), loops, match, closures, bare block\nexpressions, and other grammar remain cleanly refused.\n\nPreserve the existing expression grammar and precedence, newline continuation,\nassignment-only-at-statement-head rule, spans, and first-error funnel. Do not\ncopy Python's known grammar defects or silently consume adjacent expressions.\nIn particular, branch/else lookahead must not consume the newline needed to\nseparate the next statement. A leading minus after a newline following a closed\nif belongs to the next statement under design 259 R2. No production parser,\nmini-VM resource limit, lexer, or canonical schema changes belong here.\n\n## Representation and execution\n\nAdd an `If` arena node with empty text and ordered children: condition, then\nBlock, optional else Block. Anchor at `if`; span through its last branch.\nRepresent `else if` as an else Block containing a FinalExpression wrapping the\nnested If, matching Python's canonical shape; the synthetic block is anchored\nat the nested `if` and spans that nested expression. Existing arena invariants\nremain: backward edges, contiguous child ranges, unique child ownership,\ncomplete reachability, and parent span containment.\n\nUse one explicit parser work/continuation stack for suspended expression and\nblock work. Parsing syntactically nested ifs must not recurse through Saw/VM\ncall frames. Preserve the depth-256 expression contract and extend the same\nbudget to active nested if expressions: each active if adds one; groups,\nunary operators and argument delimiters retain their existing contributions.\nThe function body and the required branch braces do not add another charge\nfor the same if. Sequential siblings must release their budget. Pin 256/257\nfor pure if, else-if, and mixed if/group/call/unary paths, plus long shallow\nblocks/chains. Reconcile any conflict with SL-2's eventual depth convention\nexplicitly before final parity approval; never quietly change existing pins.\n\nCanonical rendering uses the existing IfExpr format: condition:, then:, and\noptional else: sections, normal Block rendering, using the renderer's iterative\nwork stack. Syntax-only acceptance must include semantically invalid conditions\nand branch value types; semantic rejection is not parser rejection.\n\n## Ownership and validation\n\nSol source agent owns `prototypes/parser/src/{lib,canonical}.saw`. Sol tests\nagent independently authors fixtures and harness checks. Sol inventory agent\nowns fresh eligibility analysis, classifier coverage and its tests. Each works\nin an isolated worktree. Parent owns this brief, review, integration, gates,\ntracker submission, and reconciliation with Claude's oracle work.\n\nTest ordinary/else-if/nested forms in every expression position; empty branches,\nstatement/tail distinctions, assignments and returns inside branches; operator\nprecedence and newline behavior; missing conditions/braces/else bodies and\nunsupported binding forms; exact spans, anchors, child order and invariants;\ndepth boundaries and long shallow inputs. Independently authored expectations\nmust not be generated from the new implementation's output.\n\nRun arena and canonical gates across VM, LLVM O0/O2, ASan, and production sawc;\nall harness tests; inventory regeneration/check; and the fresh eligible corpus\ndifferential. Report counts by verdict and compare newly eligible complete\nfiles. Existing Python disagreement remains a strict, visible debt probe, not\na tolerated divergence. Final M21 approval requires rebasing onto aligned\nPython, debt probes green, and canonical parity. If alignment has not landed,\nsubmit only as explicitly dependency-blocked work with validation limits clear.\n","id":"SL-328","labels":["prototype","selfhost","parser"],"order":0,"parent":"","priority":"normal","project":"SL","queue_order":0,"revision":12,"sequence":1366,"stage":"queued","status":"open","title":"M21: iterative control-flow parser and ordinary if/else","updated":"1790198388"},"before":{"acceptance":[],"assignee":"agent:codex","author":"agent:codex","closed":"","comments":[{"author":"agent:codex","body":"Submitted patch SL-328.p1 (revision 1): M21: iterative if/else parser (pending SL-2 alignment)","created":"1789837894","id":"c1"},{"author":"agent:codex","body":"SL-328.p1 implements ordinary if/else and else-if in every supported expression position, using an explicit expression/block continuation stack. Leading, trailing, doubled and line-ending semicolons are refused.\\n+Bare same-line juxtaposition is refused. Top-level functions take separate lines,\\n+not semicolons. These rules apply to every supported block position and retain\\n+the distinction between a final expression and a statement followed by another.\\n+\\n+Implementation and generated-driver Saw source must remain in the mini-VM's\\n+shared execution subset: use newlines rather than semicolons there. Semicolons\\n+in the embedded parser inputs exercise the new parser contract; this milestone\\n+does not extend the mini-VM frontend.\\n+\\n+## Representation and execution\\n+\\n+Add an `If` arena node with empty text and ordered children: condition, then\\n+Block, optional else Block. Anchor at `if`; span through its last branch.\\n+Represent `else if` as an else Block containing a FinalExpression wrapping the\\n+nested If, matching Python's canonical shape; the synthetic block is anchored\\n+at the nested `if` and spans that nested expression. Existing arena invariants\\n+remain: backward edges, contiguous child ranges, unique child ownership,\\n+complete reachability, and parent span containment.\\n+\\n+Use one explicit parser work/continuation stack for suspended expression and\\n+block work. Parsing syntactically nested ifs must not recurse through Saw/VM\\n+call frames. Preserve the depth-256 expression contract and extend the same\\n+budget to active nested if expressions: each active if adds one; groups,\\n+unary operators and argument delimiters retain their existing contributions.\\n+The function body and the required branch braces do not add another charge\\n+for the same if. Sequential siblings must release their budget. Pin 256/257\\n+for pure if, else-if, and mixed if/group/call/unary paths, plus long shallow\\n+blocks/chains. Reconcile any conflict with SL-2's eventual depth convention\\n+explicitly before final parity approval; never quietly change existing pins.\\n+\\n+Canonical rendering uses the existing IfExpr format: condition:, then:, and\\n+optional else: sections, normal Block rendering, using the renderer's iterative\\n+work stack. Syntax-only acceptance must include semantically invalid conditions\\n+and branch value types; semantic rejection is not parser rejection.\\n+\\n+## Ownership and validation\\n+\\n+Sol source agent owns `prototypes/parser/src/{lib,canonical}.saw`. Sol tests\\n+agent independently authors fixtures and harness checks. Sol inventory agent\\n+owns fresh eligibility analysis, classifier coverage and its tests. Each works\\n+in an isolated worktree. Parent owns this brief, review, integration, gates,\\n+tracker submission, and reconciliation with Claude's oracle work.\\n+\\n+Test ordinary/else-if/nested forms in every expression position; empty branches,\\n+statement/tail distinctions, assignments and returns inside branches; operator\\n+precedence and newline behavior; missing conditions/braces/else bodies and\\n+unsupported binding forms; exact spans, anchors, child order and invariants;\\n+depth boundaries and long shallow inputs. Independently authored expectations\\n+must not be generated from the new implementation's output.\\n+\\n+Run arena and canonical gates across VM, LLVM O0/O2, ASan, and production sawc;\\n+all harness tests; inventory regeneration/check; and the fresh eligible corpus\\n+differential. Report counts by verdict and compare newly eligible complete\\n+files. Existing Python disagreement remains a strict, visible debt probe, not\\n+a tolerated divergence. Final M21 approval requires rebasing onto aligned\\n+Python, debt probes green, and canonical parity. If alignment has not landed,\\n+submit only as explicitly dependency-blocked work with validation limits clear.\\n+\\n+The user authorized the September 23 refresh, independent gates and review to\\n+proceed before Python alignment lands. Rebase and reconcile the settled\\n+contracts now; submit the refreshed patch with its remaining dependency named.\\n+Enable applicable Python comparisons previously disabled solely for Python\\n+defects, and report their actual failures until the aligned oracle is available.\\n+Do not turn those failures into skips or tolerated discrepancies. Final approval\\n+still requires the aligned-Python rerun above. SL-73's separate general-callee\\n+`Call()` schema and casts/optional-type grammar remain outside M21.\\n+\\n+## Baseline measured September 19\\n+\\n+At base `51e30cda`, a freshly built mini-VM and the unmodified M20 comparison\\n+pass 64/64 candidates out of 2,733 tracked examples: 2,574 unsupported and 95\\n+Python parse errors. Artifacts: `.build/m21-baseline/examples/`. Later coverage\\n+claims must compare with this fresh census, not M20's historical 2,696 files.\\n+\\n+The independent M21 classifier admits 78 candidates (38 semantic negatives),\\n+with 2,560 unsupported and 95 Python parse errors. The fourteen new candidates\\n+include ordinary comparisons, nested/else-if forms, coroutine source examples,\\n+and three semantic-error programs. Eligibility is not a parity result: every\\n+candidate must still pass the actual prototype/Python comparison.\\n+\\n+## Initial implementation validation, September 19 (revision 1)\\n+\\n+All 126 arena cases pass across VM, LLVM O0/O2, ASan, and production sawc.\\n+All 35 canonical cases pass across those engines, with 22 applicable fixtures\\n+also matching Python's parse-only output. Structural arena checks pass too.\\n+All 49 Python harness tests and inventory freshness checks pass. The complete\\n+eligible-corpus differential passes 78/78 files, including all fourteen newly\\n+eligible files and all 38 semantic negatives; zero mismatches or oracle failures.\\n+\\n+Canonical validation is partitioned: 32 ordinary cases run together; the three\\n+new depth-256 if/else-if/mixed cases run individually in the VM and together\\n+across native engines. The combined three-case VM run timed out at 300 seconds.\\n+Each individual run passes with the same 300-second timeout and 120-million\\n+instruction budget. Native complete outputs agree, and every native case's\\n+status and canonical bytes match its individual VM result. No case is omitted,\\n+and no resource limit was increased. This does not establish that the default\\n+unpartitioned canonical command finishes within its timeout. Repeatable\\n+`test_canonical.py --case-prefix` selectors expose the partitions.\\n+\\n+Artifacts live under `.build/m21-validation/`: `arena-asan`,\\n+`canonical-ordinary`, `canonical-deep-if` (the timed-out combined run),\\n+`canonical-deep-partitioned`, `examples`, and `debt-probe`.\\n+\\n+The strict SL-73 debt probe still fails solely on Python's grouped-callee tree;\\n+the prototype result passes on every engine. This remains a visible dependency,\\n+with no tolerated mismatch entry. SL-328 is proposed pending SL-2 alignment,\\n+followed by rebase, depth-contract reconciliation, and parity/debt revalidation.\\n+\\n+## Timeout follow-up contract\\n+\\n+The user authorized a revision of SL-328.p1 to make canonical validation\\n+reliable by default and address the measured timeout bottleneck. The checked-in\\n+harness must partition every selected case exactly once, retain exact-byte\\n+cross-engine checks and failure artifacts, and preserve the existing per-run\\n+timeouts and instruction budgets. The ordinary default command must pass;\\n+manual selectors are no longer sufficient evidence for this revision.\\n+\\n+Measure VM startup, parsing, rendering, and framed output separately where\\n+possible, at increasing nesting depths. Optimize only the measured bottleneck\\n+within the renderer; retain the mini-VM builder's allocation-failure and\\n+snapshot contracts. Record before/after measurements, verify identical output,\\n+and keep timing evidence distinct from deterministic correctness assertions.\\n+\\n+## Timeout follow-up results (revision 2)\\n+\\n+The default canonical command now passes all 35 cases across VM, LLVM O0/O2,\\n+ASan, production sawc, and arena VM; 22 applicable fixtures also match Python.\\n+All 55 harness tests, inventory freshness, and the 78/78 whole-file differential\\n+pass. The unchanged SL-73 Python debt remains a failing strict probe and still\\n+blocks final approval pending SL-2. The earlier 126-case arena result remains\\n+applicable: the parser and arena driver did not change in this revision.\\n+\\n+The harness partitions canonical and arena VM work deterministically by case\\n+count (16) and combined source/expected-output bytes (1,000,000). An oversized\\n+case is indivisible and runs alone; its runtime guards still apply. Each run\\n+retains the existing 300-second timeout and 120-million-instruction budget.\\n+Native engines compile the complete driver once. Canonical VM batches preserve\\n+global case IDs, and their concatenated framed bytes must equal every native\\n+engine's output. A manifest, per-batch commands/output, and timings make complete\\n+coverage and failures visible. The seven canonical VM batches completed in\\n+about 9.3 seconds total; the slowest was 3.7 seconds. This supersedes revision\\n+1's reliance on manual partitioning. With the faster renderer but the old\\n+unbatched harness, the full VM driver instead reached the existing instruction\\n+limit, confirming that bounded invocations are needed as well as faster rendering.\\n+\\n+Profiling identified rendering as the bottleneck. The mini-VM builder copies\\n+existing content on each append; the old renderer appended indentation two\\n+spaces at a time directly to the full output. The revised renderer builds one\\n+complete line locally, then appends it once. Neither mini-VM behavior nor its\\n+allocation-failure and snapshot contracts changed.\\n+\\n+The finalized profiler's matched depth-128 comparison used three samples per\\n+phase, identical capture/validation, and the same VM binary:\\n+\\n+| Cumulative median, seconds | Before | After |\\n+|---|---:|---:|\\n+| Parse (including VM startup and source construction) | 0.174 | 0.163 |\\n+| Parse + render | 5.969 | 0.277 |\\n+| Parse + render + decimal output | 6.186 | 0.428 |\\n+\\n+Subtracting cumulative medians estimates rendering at 5.795 versus 0.114 seconds\\n+(about 51 times faster). Subtraction has measurement noise; these are report-only\\n+measurements, not correctness thresholds. Exploratory increasing-depth probes\\n+identified the scaling issue; the matched finalized comparison supports the\\n+speedup claim. `profile_canonical.py` records renderer/source hashes and commands,\\n+persists results incrementally, supports a baseline `--canonical` path, and\\n+rejects error markers even when followed by a completion marker.\\n+\\n+Revision 2 gate artifacts are under `.build/m21-validation-r2/`, including the\\n+canonical batch manifest and timings, whole-file comparison, strict debt probe,\\n+and copied finalized profiling results in `profile-before-128` and\\n+`profile-after-128`.\\n+\\n+## Settled-contract refresh, September 23 (revision 3)\\n+\\n+The refresh is based on `52b92cc6`, which includes the merged SL-350 compiler\\n+fix. Three Sol agents implemented the parser boundary, independently authored\\n+fixtures/harness updates, and inventory classifier changes in separate\\n+worktrees. The lead integrated and ran the gates with that fixed compiler.\\n+The old M21 worktree and production parser were not modified.\\n+\\n+The default arena gate passes all 141 cases across VM, LLVM O0/O2, ASan and\\n+production sawc, including the unchanged 256/257 depth boundaries. All 38\\n+canonical cases pass across those engines and the canonical harness's arena-VM\\n+checks. Python comparisons are now enabled for every case previously excluded\\n+solely for a Python defect. Of 37 applicable comparisons, 28 match and nine\\n+fail: grouped-identifier calls, binary-operand newline continuation, and seven\\n+depth-256 cases (groups, calls, assignment-target groups, assignment-RHS groups,\\n+pure if, else-if and mixed nesting). The seven depth failures end in Python\\n+`RecursionError`. Unary-256 and both long shallow chains already match.\\n+\\n+The strict grouped-call debt probe still fails. The harness suite passes 56 of\\n+58 tests; its two failures enforce the same pending Python contracts, through\\n+canonical comparison and grouped-call inventory eligibility. No skip, xfail or\\n+tolerated mismatch was introduced. The old inventory guard that classified\\n+every `)(` token pair as unresolved was removed: eligibility now follows the\\n+actual parser and AST/source audits rather than preserving Python's old defect.\\n+The general-callee renderer refusal remains an explicit out-of-scope boundary.\\n+\\n+The fresh census covers 2,824 examples: 78 candidates, 2,638 unsupported files\\n+and 108 Python parse errors. All 78 candidate files compare successfully,\\n+including 38 semantic negatives. Candidate paths are unchanged from revision 2;\\n+one candidate source changed and was compared again. Snapshot freshness passes.\\n+\\n+The first full arena attempt hit the existing 300-second clang O2 compile\\n+limit.
